GET /permissions-service/v1/permissions/principals?project_name=…

Lists the IDs of principals with grants in the project. The response has principals (string[]) and pagination. It takes pagination and search.

TypeScriptcURL 
for await (const id of permio.listPrincipals()) console.log(id);

curl "$PERMIO_API/permissions-service/v1/permissions/principals?project_name=default" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $PERMIO_API_KEY"

docs.title: GetAllAssignmentsForPrincipal
docs.text:
GET /permissions-service/v1/permissions/assignments/principal/{principal_id=**}?project_name=…

Lists every grant a principal has in the project. The response has assignments (Assignment[]) and pagination. Principal IDs may contain slashes.

TypeScriptcURL 
for await (const a of permio.listAssignments({ principal: "alice" })) {
  console.log(a.resourceUri, a.permissions.map((p) => p.name), a.roles.map((r) => r.name));
}

curl "$PERMIO_API/permissions-service/v1/permissions/assignments/principal/alice?project_name=default" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $PERMIO_API_KEY"

docs.title: Access queries
docs.text: These answer "where?" and "who?" instead of "may they?", with the same rules as Check. The guide Filtering lists and building share dialogs shows how to use them.

docs.title: ListAccess
docs.text:
GET /permissions-service/v1/access?project_name=…&principal_id=…&permission=…&under_uri=…

Answers "where can this principal use this permission, at or below under_uri?". It counts grants made to the principal directly, through roles, and through the groups it is a member of. perms.io doesn't know your records, so the answer is a list of scopes in your URI tree, not a list of objects:

  • If the principal holds the permission on under_uri itself (through a grant on it, on an ancestor, or on a stored _ wildcard URI that matches it), covers_all is true and scopes is a single SUBTREE scope for under_uri. There are no further pages.
  • Otherwise scopes lists the URIs of the grants below under_uri that confer the permission. A concrete URI is a SUBTREE scope, because a grant applies to its URI and everything below it. A URI with _ wildcard segments is a PATTERN scope. Scopes are ordered by uri and paginated.

Needs: permission.check on under_uri, and principal.assignment.get on the principal.

Request (ListAccessRequest)

Field Type Description project_name string Required. principal_id string Required. permission string Required. One permission name. under_uri string Required. Only resources at or below this URI are considered. A _ segment here is literal. pagination PaginationRequest Optional.

Response (ListAccessResponse)

Field Type Description covers_all bool true if the principal holds the permission on under_uri itself, and so on everything below it. scopes AccessScope[] The places at or below under_uri where the principal holds the permission, ordered by uri. pagination PaginationResponse next_cursor for the next page.

AccessScope

Field Type Description uri string A resource URI (SUBTREE, EXACT) or a URI pattern with _ segments (PATTERN). For a grant below under_uri, it is the URI the grant was made on, which may have _ segments in the part that matches under_uri. scope AccessScopeKind Which resources uri stands for.

AccessScopeKind

Value Meaning ACCESS_SCOPE_KIND_SUBTREE The resource uri and every resource below it. ACCESS_SCOPE_KIND_PATTERN Every resource whose leading segments match uri, where each _ segment matches exactly one segment, and every resource below those. ACCESS_SCOPE_KIND_EXACT Exactly the resource uri. Reserved: grants are always inherited, so it isn't returned today.

To filter a database by a SUBTREE scope p, match path = p or path starting with p/. A bare prefix match on p would also match siblings such as /documents/12 for /documents/1.

Errors: INVALID_ARGUMENT for a malformed request or an invalid cursor; PERMISSION_DENIED if the API key lacks either permission; NOT_FOUND if principal_id is group:<slug> and that group doesn't exist.

TypeScriptcURLGoPython 
const access = await permio.listAccess({
  principal: "alice",
  permission: "document.read",
  under: "/documents",
});
access.coversAll;    // false
access.toPrefixes(); // ["/documents/4", "/documents/7"]

Available from SDK 0.2.0. It follows every page. See listAccess.

curl "$PERMIO_API/permissions-service/v1/access?project_name=default&principal_id=alice&permission=document.read&under_uri=/documents" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $PERMIO_API_KEY"

{"scopes": [
  {"uri": "/documents/4", "scope": "ACCESS_SCOPE_KIND_SUBTREE"},
  {"uri": "/documents/7", "scope": "ACCESS_SCOPE_KIND_SUBTREE"}
]}

res, err := client.ListAccess(ctx, &permissionsv1.ListAccessRequest{
    ProjectName: "default",
    PrincipalId: "alice",
    Permission:  "document.read",
    UnderUri:    "/documents",
})
// handle err
if res.GetCoversAll() {
    // no filter needed
}
for _, s := range res.GetScopes() {
    if s.GetScope() == permissionsv1.AccessScopeKind_ACCESS_SCOPE_KIND_SUBTREE {
        fmt.Println(s.GetUri())
    }
}

res = client.ListAccess(
    permissions_pb2.ListAccessRequest(
        project_name="default",
        principal_id="alice",
        permission="document.read",
        under_uri="/documents",
    ),
    metadata=[("authorization", f"Bearer {api_key}")],
)
for s in res.scopes:
    if s.scope == permissions_pb2.ACCESS_SCOPE_KIND_SUBTREE:
        print(s.uri)

docs.title: ListPrincipalsWithAccess
docs.text:
GET /permissions-service/v1/access/principals?project_name=…&resource_uri=…

Answers "who has access to resource_uri?". It lists the principals with a grant on the resource, on an ancestor of it, or on a stored _ wildcard URI that matches it, with the grants that give the access.

  • With permission set, only grants that confer that permission count, so a principal is listed exactly when a Check for it passes through its own grants. Without it, every grant with at least one permission or role counts.
  • Groups are listed as principals, with is_group set. With expand_groups, each group's members are listed too, once per group, with via_group set.
  • Entries are ordered by principal_id, then via_group, and paginated.

Needs: principal.list and principal.assignment.list on the project.

Request (ListPrincipalsWithAccessRequest)

Field Type Description project_name string Required. resource_uri string Required. The resource to look at. A _ segment here is literal. permission string Optional. Only count grants that confer this permission. expand_groups bool Optional. Also list the members of every listed group. pagination PaginationRequest Optional.

Response (ListPrincipalsWithAccessResponse): principals (PrincipalAccess[]) and pagination.

PrincipalAccess

Field Type Description principal_id string The principal. A group appears as group:<slug>. is_group bool true if principal_id is a group. via_group string For entries added by expand_groups: the slug of the group through which the principal holds the grants in via. Empty for grants made to the principal itself. via AccessGrant[] The grants that give the access, most specific first.

AccessGrant

Field Type Description resource_uri string The URI the grant was made on: the resource itself, an ancestor, or a URI with _ segments that matches it. inherited bool true unless the grant was made on exactly the resource. match AccessGrantMatch ACCESS_GRANT_MATCH_EXACT (on the resource), ACCESS_GRANT_MATCH_ANCESTOR (on an ancestor, possibly with _ segments) or ACCESS_GRANT_MATCH_WILDCARD (same depth, with _ segments). role AccessGrantRole Set when the access comes through a role: its id and name. direct AccessGrantDirect Set (as an empty message) when the access comes from directly granted permissions.

role and direct are a oneof called source: exactly one is set.

Errors: INVALID_ARGUMENT for a malformed request or an invalid cursor; PERMISSION_DENIED if the API key lacks either permission.

TypeScriptcURL 
const entries = await permio.whoHasAccess({
  resource: "/documents/42",
  permission: "document.read",
  expandGroups: true,
});

Available from SDK 0.2.0. It follows every page. See whoHasAccess.

curl "$PERMIO_API/permissions-service/v1/access/principals?project_name=default&resource_uri=/documents/42&permission=document.read&expand_groups=true" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $PERMIO_API_KEY"

{"principals": [
  {"principalId": "alice",
   "via": [{"resourceUri": "/documents", "inherited": true, "match": "ACCESS_GRANT_MATCH_ANCESTOR",
            "role": {"id": "ROLE_ID", "name": "viewer"}}]},
  {"principalId": "bob", "viaGroup": "editors",
   "via": [{"resourceUri": "/documents", "inherited": true, "match": "ACCESS_GRANT_MATCH_ANCESTOR", "direct": {}}]},
  {"principalId": "group:editors", "isGroup": true,
   "via": [{"resourceUri": "/documents", "inherited": true, "match": "ACCESS_GRANT_MATCH_ANCESTOR", "direct": {}}]}
]}

docs.title: Groups
docs.text:
A group is a named set of principals in a project. Grant to its principal ID, group:<slug>, with GrantUserPermissionsAndRolesOnResource, and every member holds the grant. Groups can't contain groups.

In the paths below, {name} is the group's slug: 1–64 characters, lowercase letters, digits and -.

Group

Field Type Description id string Unique ID. organisation_id string Owning organisation. project_name string Owning project. name string The slug, unique within the project. It can't be changed. description string Free text, up to 1024 characters. principal_id string The principal ID grants to the group are made to: group:<name>. created_at, updated_at Timestamp

GroupMember: principal_id (string) and created_at (Timestamp, when the principal was added).

docs.title: CreateGroup
docs.text:
POST /permissions-service/v1/groups

Creates a group and returns the Group. Returns ALREADY_EXISTS if the project already has a group with this name.

Needs: group.create on the project.

Field Type Description project_name string Required. name string Required. The slug. description string Optional. Up to 1024 characters. TypeScriptcURLGoPython 
const g = await permio.groups.create("editors", { description: "Can edit every document" });
g.principalId; // "group:editors"

curl -X POST "$PERMIO_API/permissions-service/v1/groups" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $PERMIO_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"project_name": "default", "name": "editors", "description": "Can edit every document"}'

g, err := client.CreateGroup(ctx, &permissionsv1.CreateGroupRequest{
    ProjectName: "default",
    Name:        "editors",
    Description: "Can edit every document",
})

g = client.CreateGroup(
    permissions_pb2.CreateGroupRequest(project_name="default", name="editors", description="Can edit every document"),
    metadata=[("authorization", f"Bearer {api_key}")],
)

docs.title: GetGroup
docs.text:
GET /permissions-service/v1/groups/{name}?project_name=…

Returns a Group, or NOT_FOUND.

Needs: group.get on the group.

TypeScriptcURL 
const g = await permio.groups.get("editors");

curl "$PERMIO_API/permissions-service/v1/groups/editors?project_name=default" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $PERMIO_API_KEY"

docs.title: UpdateGroup
docs.text:
PUT /permissions-service/v1/groups/{name}

Replaces a group's description and returns the updated Group, or NOT_FOUND. The name can't be changed, because group:<name> is the principal ID its grants are stored under.

Needs: group.update on the group.

Field Type Description project_name string Required. name string Required (path). description string The new description. Up to 1024 characters. TypeScriptcURL 
await permio.groups.update("editors", { description: "Edits documents and comments" });

curl -X PUT "$PERMIO_API/permissions-service/v1/groups/editors" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $PERMIO_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"project_name": "default", "description": "Edits documents and comments"}'

docs.title: DeleteGroup
docs.text:
DELETE /permissions-service/v1/groups/{name}?project_name=…

Deletes a group together with its memberships and every grant made to it, in one transaction. This call is idempotent: it succeeds whether or not the group existed.

Needs: group.delete on the group, and principal.assignment.delete on the project, because it revokes the group's grants.

TypeScriptcURL 
await permio.groups.delete("editors");

curl -X DELETE "$PERMIO_API/permissions-service/v1/groups/editors?project_name=default" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $PERMIO_API_KEY"

docs.title: ListGroups
docs.text:
GET /permissions-service/v1/groups?project_name=…

Lists the groups in a project, ordered by name. The response has groups (Group[]) and pagination. It takes pagination and search (filters by name, up to 128 characters).

Needs: group.list on the project.

TypeScriptcURL 
for await (const g of permio.groups.list({ search: "edit" })) console.log(g.name);

curl "$PERMIO_API/permissions-service/v1/groups?project_name=default&search=edit" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $PERMIO_API_KEY"

docs.title: AddGroupMembers
docs.text:
POST /permissions-service/v1/groups/{name}/members/add

Adds up to 100 principals to a group. Principals that are already members are reported, not added again. A principal that is new to your organisation counts towards its unique principals, exactly as if it had been granted something, and goes through the same billing check.

Needs: group.member.add on the group and principal.assignment.create on the project. A member gets the group's grants anywhere in the project, so only a caller who could grant that access directly may add members.

Field Type Description project_name string Required. name string Required (path). principal_ids string[] Required. 1–100 unique principal IDs. They may not start with group:.

Response (AddGroupMembersResponse)

Field Type Description added_principal_ids string[] The principals that were added, in request order. existing_principal_ids string[] The principals that were already members, in request order.

Errors: INVALID_ARGUMENT if a principal ID starts with group: (groups can't be nested); NOT_FOUND if the group doesn't exist; PERMISSION_DENIED if the caller lacks either permission, or if the organisation may not add new principals.

TypeScriptcURLGoPython 
const { added, existing } = await permio.groups.addMembers("editors", ["alice", "bob"]);

curl -X POST "$PERMIO_API/permissions-service/v1/groups/editors/members/add" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $PERMIO_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"project_name": "default", "principal_ids": ["alice", "bob"]}'

{"addedPrincipalIds": ["alice", "bob"]}

res, err := client.AddGroupMembers(ctx, &permissionsv1.AddGroupMembersRequest{
    ProjectName:  "default",
    Name:         "editors",
    PrincipalIds: []string{"alice", "bob"},
})

res = client.AddGroupMembers(
    permissions_pb2.AddGroupMembersRequest(project_name="default", name="editors", principal_ids=["alice", "bob"]),
    metadata=[("authorization", f"Bearer {api_key}")],
)

docs.title: RemoveGroupMembers
docs.text:
POST /permissions-service/v1/groups/{name}/members/remove

Removes up to 100 principals from a group. Principals that aren't members are reported. It takes the same fields as AddGroupMembers.

Needs: group.member.remove on the group and principal.assignment.create on the project.

Response (RemoveGroupMembersResponse): removed_principal_ids and not_member_principal_ids (string[], in request order).

TypeScriptcURL 
const { removed, notMembers } = await permio.groups.removeMembers("editors", ["bob"]);

curl -X POST "$PERMIO_API/permissions-service/v1/groups/editors/members/remove" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $PERMIO_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"project_name": "default", "principal_ids": ["bob"]}'

docs.title: ListGroupMembers
docs.text:
GET /permissions-service/v1/groups/{name}/members?project_name=…

Lists a group's members, ordered by principal ID. The response has members (GroupMember[]) and pagination. It takes pagination.

Needs: group.member.list on the group.

TypeScriptcURL 
for await (const m of permio.groups.listMembers("editors")) console.log(m.principalId);

curl "$PERMIO_API/permissions-service/v1/groups/editors/members?project_name=default" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $PERMIO_API_KEY"

docs.title: ListGroupsForPrincipal
docs.text:
GET /permissions-service/v1/group-memberships/{principal_id=**}?project_name=…

Lists the groups a principal is a member of in the project, ordered by name. The response has groups (Group[]) and pagination. It takes pagination. Principal IDs may contain slashes.

Needs: group.list on the project, and principal.assignment.list on the principal.

TypeScriptcURL 
for await (const g of permio.groups.listForPrincipal("alice")) console.log(g.name);

curl "$PERMIO_API/permissions-service/v1/group-memberships/alice?project_name=default" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $PERMIO_API_KEY"

docs.title: API keys
docs.text: Your backend authenticates to the perms.io API with an API key. Each key belongs to one project.

docs.title: Creating a key
docs.text:
In the dashboard, pick the project in the project switcher, open API Keys and click Create New Key. Give the key a name, ideally after the service or environment that will use it, and click Create key.

Shown once

The full key is only shown once, when it is created. Copy it into your secrets manager straight away. perms.io only stores a hash of the key, so it can't show it to you again. If you lose a key, create a new one and invalidate the old one.

docs.title: Format
docs.text:
Keys are opaque, 44-character strings:

perms_ + 32 random base62 characters + 6-character checksum
  • The perms_ prefix makes leaked keys easy for secret scanners to spot.
  • The last 6 characters are a CRC32 checksum of the random part. Clients can use them to reject a mistyped or truncated key before sending it. The TypeScript SDK does this in its constructor.
  • The checksum only catches typos. Whether a key exists and is still valid is decided by the API.

Older keys were issued as JWTs. These are still accepted.

docs.title: Sending a key
docs.text:
Send the key as a bearer token on every request:

HTTPgRPC metadata 
Authorization: Bearer perms_...

authorization: Bearer perms_...

A request with a missing, unknown or invalidated key is rejected with Unauthenticated (HTTP 401).

docs.title: Access levels
docs.text:
A key is a principal in its own right. When it is created, the key is granted a role on its project, and that role decides which calls the key may make.

Access Role Allows Check (default) apikey.checker Check, BatchCheck, ListAccess and ListPrincipalsWithAccess. Reading permissions, roles, principals, assignments, groups and group members (permission.check, permission.get, permission.list, role.get, role.list, principal.list, principal.assignment.get, principal.assignment.list, group.get, group.list, group.member.list). Full access apikey.manager Everything above, plus creating, updating and deleting permissions, roles and groups, granting and revoking, and adding and removing group members (permission.create/update/delete, role.create/update/delete, principal.assignment.create/delete, group.create/update/delete, group.member.add/remove).

Each RPC's level is listed in the API reference.

docs.title: Choosing the level
docs.text:
The level is set when the key is created, with the access field of CreateAPIKey:

access Level API_KEY_ACCESS_CHECK Check. API_KEY_ACCESS_FULL Full access. API_KEY_ACCESS_UNSPECIFIED (or left out) Check.

The key's access field reports its level when you list keys. A key's level can't be changed later: create a new key with the level you need and invalidate the old one.

To create a key with a given level, you must hold every permission that level grants on the project, so nobody can create a key with more access than they have. Otherwise the call fails with PERMISSION_DENIED. Choosing the level when creating a key in the dashboard is being added. Until it is available there, keys created in the dashboard get check access.

Give a key the least access it needs. A service that only checks permissions, filters lists or shows who has access needs only check access. Use full access for services that manage permissions, roles, grants or groups.

A call the key isn't allowed to make is rejected with PermissionDenied (HTTP 403). This is about the key's rights, not the principal you are checking. For Check, the key needs permission.check on the checked resources and on the principal, which the check role gives it across its whole project.

Neither role includes organisation-level permissions. Most Organisation service calls are meant for the dashboard and will be denied for an API key.

docs.title: Invalidating a key
docs.text:
On the API Keys page, click Invalidate next to the key and confirm. The key stops working immediately and this can't be undone. Its grants on the project are removed too. Invalidated keys stay listed, marked Invalidated.

Keys created in the dashboard don't expire, so invalidate any key you no longer need.

docs.title: Good practice
docs.text:
• Use one key per service and environment, so you can invalidate one without affecting the others.
  • Keep keys on the server. Never ship a key in browser or mobile code: anyone who loads the page can read it.
  • Store keys in a secrets manager or environment variables, not in source control.

docs.title: Groups
docs.text:
A group is a named set of principals in a project. You grant permissions and roles to the group once, and every member holds them. Use groups for teams, departments or any set of users that should share access, instead of repeating the same grants for each user.

group:editors  ── document.write on /documents
   ├── alice   ✔ can write /documents/42
   └── bob     ✔ can write /documents/42

docs.title: The group:<slug> principal
docs.text:
Each group has a slug, its name: 1–64 lower-case letters, digits and hyphens, unique within the project. Grants to the group are made to the principal ID group:<slug>. You use it exactly like any other principal ID when you grant, revoke or list assignments:

TypeScriptcURL 
import { group } from "permio";

await permio.permissions.grantUserPermissionsAndRolesOnResource({
  projectName: "default",
  userId: group("editors"), // "group:editors"
  resourceUri: "/documents",
  permissions: ["document.write"],
});

curl -X POST "$PERMIO_API/permissions-service/v1/permissions/assign" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $PERMIO_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"project_name": "default", "user_id": "group:editors", "resource_uri": "/documents", "permissions": ["document.write"]}'

The group: prefix is reserved:

  • A grant to group:<slug> is only accepted if that group exists in the project. Otherwise the call fails with NOT_FOUND. A group: ID that isn't a valid slug is rejected with INVALID_ARGUMENT.
  • Revoking from a group: principal always works, even if the group no longer exists, so stray grants can be cleaned up.
  • A group: ID can never be a member of a group.

docs.title: Groups belong to a project
docs.text: Like permissions, roles and grants, a group belongs to one project. Its members and its grants only apply in that project. Two projects can each have a group called editors, and they are unrelated.

docs.title: Members
docs.text:
A member is any principal ID, the same IDs you pass to a check. perms.io doesn't need to know the principal in advance. You add and remove up to 100 members per call. The response tells you which principals were added and which were already members (or, when removing, which weren't members).

Groups are flat: a group can't contain another group. Adding a group: principal as a member is rejected with INVALID_ARGUMENT.

You can also see the groups a principal belongs to (ListGroupsForPrincipal), and list a group's members.

docs.title: How checks use groups
docs.text:
When you check a principal, perms.io counts the principal's own grants and the grants of every group it is a member of in that project. Nothing changes in your code: you still check alice, and access she has through group:editors counts.

The same rules apply everywhere else a check is answered: BatchCheck and ListAccess include the principal's groups too. ListPrincipalsWithAccess lists the group itself, and with expand_groups also lists its members. See Filtering lists and building share dialogs.

Membership changes apply to the next check straight away. Adding alice to editors gives her the group's grants everywhere in the project, including grants made to the group later.

docs.title: Changing and deleting a group
docs.text:
• No renaming. A group's slug can't be changed, because group:<slug> is the principal ID its grants are stored under. You can change its description. To rename, create a new group, grant it the same access, move the members and delete the old one.
  • Deleting a group also removes all its memberships and every grant made to group:<slug>, in one transaction. Members keep any access they have through their own grants or other groups. Deleting a group that doesn't exist succeeds.

docs.title: Billing
docs.text:
Groups don't count towards your plan's unique principals. Their members do: a principal that is a member of a group counts as a unique principal, just as if it had been granted something directly. A principal is counted once, however many groups and grants it has.

Adding a member who is new to your organisation goes through the same billing check as granting to a new principal. If your organisation isn't allowed to add principals, the call fails with PERMISSION_DENIED.

docs.title: Permissions you need
docs.text:
Managing groups needs these permissions on the project. In the dashboard they come with your organisation role. For an API key, see Access levels.

Action Needs Create a group group.create View or list groups and members group.get, group.list, group.member.list Change a description group.update Delete a group group.delete, plus principal.assignment.delete, because it revokes the group's grants Add or remove members group.member.add / group.member.remove, plus principal.assignment.create on the whole project Grant to a group The same as any grant: principal.assignment.create on the resource

Changing membership requires the right to grant across the whole project because a member gets the group's grants anywhere in the project. Only someone who could already grant that access directly can add members. This stops group membership from being used to get around the limits on who may grant what.

A check-access API key can read groups and members. Creating, changing and deleting groups and changing membership needs a full-access key.

docs.title: Managing groups
docs.text:
• Dashboard: use the Groups page in the dashboard to create groups and manage their members.
  • TypeScript SDK: permio.groups (available from 0.2.0). See Groups.
  • API: the group RPCs in the API reference.
await permio.groups.create("editors", { description: "Can edit every document" });
await permio.groups.addMembers("editors", ["alice", "bob"]);
// grant to group("editors") as above, then:
await permio.check({ principal: "alice", resource: "/documents/42", permission: "document.write" }); // true

docs.title: Resources and inheritance
docs.text:
Every grant and every check in perms.io names a resource URI. A resource URI is a /-separated path that you choose to identify something in your application. Your URIs don't need to match your app's real URLs; they only need to be consistent.

/documents
/documents/42
/documents/42/comments/7
/tenants/acme/projects/web-app

docs.title: Rules for URIs
docs.text:
A resource URI:

  • starts with /;
  • has no empty segments, so no // and no trailing /;
  • contains no whitespace or control characters;
  • is at most 2048 bytes long;
  • contains none of these characters in any segment: ( ) [ ] { } * + ? | ^ $ \.

A request that breaks these rules is rejected with InvalidArgument. If your IDs can contain reserved characters, percent-encode each segment. The TypeScript SDK's resource() helper does this for you.

docs.title: Grants apply to everything beneath them
docs.text:
A grant on a URI applies to that URI and every URI below it. Matching works segment by segment, so a grant on /documents covers /documents/42 but not /documents-archive.

/documents                  ← grant document.read to alice here
├── /documents/42           ✔ alice can read
│   └── /documents/42/comments/7   ✔ alice can read
└── /documents/43           ✔ alice can read
/invoices/1                 ✘ not covered
Grant on Check on Result /documents /documents allowed /documents /documents/42 allowed /documents /documents/42/comments/7 allowed /documents/42 /documents denied (grants don't flow upwards) /documents /invoices/1 denied

Inheritance also covers resources that didn't exist when the grant was made. Grant on a tenant or a folder once, and everything you later create beneath it is covered.

docs.title: The _ wildcard segment
docs.text:
A segment that is exactly _ in a stored grant matches exactly one segment, whatever its value:

Grant on Check on Result /documents/_/comments /documents/42/comments allowed /documents/_/comments /documents/42/comments/7 allowed (beneath a match) /documents/_/comments /documents/42 denied (the grant is deeper) /documents/_/comments /documents/42/attachments denied

In a URI being checked, _ is literal. It is not a wildcard, and it only matches grants made with _ in that position. You can't widen a check by sending _.

docs.title: How a check is decided
docs.text:
A check asks: does principal P hold every permission in a list on every resource in a list, within one project?

  1. A permission counts if the principal holds it directly, or through a role, in a grant on the resource or on any ancestor of it (including _ matches).
  2. If every permission is held on every resource, the check passes (passed: true).
  3. Otherwise it fails (passed: false) and missing_permissions lists, per resource, the permissions that weren't found.

A failed check is a normal response, not an error. Checks fail closed: a URI with no applicable grant is denied.

Grants belong to a project. A check in one project never sees grants made in another.

docs.title: Designing your URIs
docs.text:
• Put the thing you grant on at the top. If you usually grant per tenant, start URIs with the tenant: /tenants/{tenantId}/....
  • Use stable IDs, not names that can change.
  • Build URIs the same way everywhere. A grant on /Documents/42 doesn't cover /documents/42.
  • Check the most specific URI for the object being accessed. Inheritance takes care of broader grants.
/tenants/acme                         ← tenant admins
/tenants/acme/projects/web-app        ← project members
/tenants/acme/projects/web-app/documents/42   ← what your code checks

docs.title: Filtering lists and building share dialogs
docs.text:
Check answers one question about one object. Lists and share dialogs need different questions:

You want to… Use SDK (from 0.2.0) Show only the rows a user may see, filtered in your database ListAccess listAccess() → toPrefixes(), toRegExp() Filter rows you already loaded ListAccess, or BatchCheck allows(), batchCheck() Show who can access an object ListPrincipalsWithAccess whoHasAccess()

All three apply exactly the same rules as Check: inheritance, the _ wildcard, roles and groups.

The examples use the TypeScript SDK. The methods on this page are available from 0.2.0. The API reference has the same calls over REST and gRPC.

docs.title: Permio returns scopes, not records
docs.text:
perms.io doesn't know your rows. It only knows the grants you made. So ListAccess can't return "documents 4, 7 and 9". It returns scopes: the places in your URI tree where the principal holds the permission.

Because a grant applies to its URI and everything beneath it, each scope stands for a whole subtree. A grant on /foo/bar gives the scope /foo/bar, and it covers /foo/bar, /foo/bar/baz and anything later created below it. Your code turns the scopes into a filter on your own data.

grants for alice (document.read)       scopes under /documents
  /documents/4                    →      /documents/4    SUBTREE
  /documents/7                    →      /documents/7    SUBTREE
  /documents/_/comments           →      /documents/_/comments   PATTERN

There are three possible answers:

  • coversAll: the principal holds the permission on the under URI itself, so on everything below it. Don't filter at all.
  • SUBTREE scopes: a URI and everything below it. These turn into prefix filters.
  • PATTERN scopes: a grant made on a URI with _ wildcard segments, such as /documents/_/comments. Each _ matches exactly one segment, and everything below a match is covered too. No prefix can express this, so use toRegExp() or filter in memory with allows().

To use any of the filters below, store each row's resource URI (here in a path column), built the same way as when you grant, for example with resource().

docs.title: Ask once with listAccess
docs.text:
import { Permio } from "permio";

const permio = new Permio({ apiKey: process.env.PERMIO_API_KEY!, project: "default" });

const access = await permio.listAccess({
  principal: userId,
  permission: "document.read",
  under: "/documents", // only resources at or below this URI are considered
});

listAccess follows every page and returns an AccessScopes object. The parts you use for filtering:

Member Use coversAll true: no filter needed. Check it first. toPrefixes() The SUBTREE URIs. Prefixes already covered by a shorter one are dropped. hasPatterns / patterns() Whether there are PATTERN scopes, and their URIs. toRegExp() One anchored RegExp that matches exactly the covered URIs, patterns included. allows(uri) Whether one URI is covered.

The answer is only about resources at or below under. For a URI outside under, allows() returning false means "not asked", not "denied".

Match on segment boundaries

A prefix p stands for p itself and everything below it. Match path = p OR path starts with p + '/'. A bare "starts with p" is wrong: the scope /documents/1 would also match /documents/12.

Don't use LIKE p || '%' either. In SQL LIKE, _ and % are wildcards, and _ is common in IDs, so it matches rows it shouldn't unless you escape them.

docs.title: PostgreSQL
docs.text:
starts_with (PostgreSQL 11+) compares literally, so it is safe with any ID:

const prefixes = access.toPrefixes();
const { rows } = access.coversAll
  ? await pool.query("SELECT * FROM documents")
  : await pool.query(
      `SELECT * FROM documents
        WHERE path = ANY($1::text[])
           OR EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM unnest($1::text[]) AS p WHERE starts_with(path, p || '/'))
           OR ($2::text IS NOT NULL AND path ~ $2)`,
      [prefixes, access.hasPatterns ? access.toRegExp().source : null],
    );

The last condition handles PATTERN scopes. toRegExp().source is valid PostgreSQL regular-expression syntax. On its own, path ~ $1 with toRegExp().source also works for every scope, but it can't use an index.

docs.title: Prisma
docs.text:
Prisma's startsWith is literal, so the boundary match is safe:

let docs: Document[];
if (access.coversAll) {
  docs = await prisma.document.findMany();
} else if (!access.hasPatterns) {
  const prefixes = access.toPrefixes();
  docs = await prisma.document.findMany({
    where: { OR: [{ path: { in: prefixes } }, ...prefixes.map((p) => ({ path: { startsWith: p + "/" } }))] },
  });
} else {
  // Prisma has no portable regex filter: load the candidates under /documents and keep the allowed ones.
  const candidates = await prisma.document.findMany({ where: { path: { startsWith: "/documents/" } } });
  docs = candidates.filter((d) => access.allows(d.path));
}

If your rows have only an ID and their URI is /documents/<id>, the prefixes exactly one segment below under are the IDs the user can read (when hasPatterns is false; a pattern such as /documents/_ stands for every document):

const ids = access
  .toPrefixes()
  .filter((p) => p.split("/").length === 3)
  .map((p) => decodeURIComponent(p.split("/")[2]!));
const docs = access.coversAll
  ? await prisma.document.findMany()
  : await prisma.document.findMany({ where: { id: { in: ids } } });

A deeper prefix such as /documents/7/comments gives access below document 7, not to document 7 itself, so it is rightly left out.

docs.title: MongoDB
docs.text:
toRegExp() covers SUBTREE, PATTERN and EXACT scopes in one anchored regular expression:

const filter = access.coversAll ? {} : { path: access.toRegExp() };
const docs = await db.collection("documents").find(filter).toArray();

With no scopes at all, toRegExp() matches nothing.

docs.title: allows() in memory
docs.text:
When the rows are already loaded, test each URI against the scopes. The number of calls to perms.io doesn't depend on how many rows you have, and allows() handles PATTERN scopes:

import { resource } from "permio";

const visible = docs.filter((d) => access.allows(resource("documents", d.id)));

docs.title: batchCheck for a fetched page
docs.text:
For a short list, such as one page of search results, batchCheck checks every resource separately and returns a Map from URI to true/false:

const uris = docs.map((d) => resource("documents", d.id));
const allowed = await permio.batchCheck({ principal: userId, resources: uris, permission: "document.read" });
const visible = docs.filter((d) => allowed.get(resource("documents", d.id)));
  • A resource is allowed only if the principal holds every listed permission on it.
  • Each API call takes up to 100 resources. The SDK splits longer lists into parallel calls.
  • batchCheckDetailed returns { resource, allowed, missing } for each resource, in request order.

Filtering after fetching means a page can come back with fewer rows than you asked for. When you need full pages, filter in the database with listAccess.

API key access

batchCheck needs permission.check, like check. listAccess also needs principal.assignment.get on the principal. A check-access key has both.

docs.title: Build a share dialog with whoHasAccess
docs.text:
A share dialog shows who can already open an object. whoHasAccess lists every principal with a grant on the resource, on an ancestor of it, or on a _ wildcard URI that matches it, with the grants that give the access:

const entries = await permio.whoHasAccess({
  resource: "/documents/42",
  permission: "document.read", // optional: only grants that confer this permission
  expandGroups: true,          // also list each group's members
});

for (const e of entries) {
  const how = e.via
    .map((g) => (g.source.type === "role" ? g.source.name : "direct") + (g.inherited ? ` from ${g.resource}` : ""))
    .join(", ");
  console.log(e.principal, e.isGroup ? "(group)" : "", e.viaGroup ? `via ${e.viaGroup}` : "", how);
}
// For example:
// alice  viewer from /documents
// group:editors (group)  direct
// bob  via editors  direct

Each entry (AccessEntry) has:

Field Meaning principal The principal ID. Groups appear as group:<slug>. isGroup true for a group. viaGroup For entries added by expandGroups: the slug of the group the access comes through. undefined for the principal's own grants. via The grants that give the access, most specific first: resource (where the grant was made), inherited, match ("exact", "ancestor" or "wildcard") and source (a role with its id and name, or "direct").

Tips for the dialog:

  • Pass permission. A principal is then listed exactly when a check for it passes through its own grants, and an entry with viaGroup exactly when it passes through that group. Without permission, any grant on the resource or above counts, whatever it allows.
  • Without expandGroups, group members aren't listed; only the group is. With it, a member of two groups appears once per group, so de-duplicate by principal if you show people once.
  • Use inherited and resource to show "inherited from /documents" and to send people to the right place to change it. Revoking on /documents/42 doesn't remove a grant made on /documents.
  • Entries are ordered by principal ID.

whoHasAccess needs principal.list and principal.assignment.list on the project, which a check-access key has.

docs.title: Choosing an approach
docs.text: Situation Approach Paginated list from your database listAccess + toPrefixes() (and toRegExp() if hasPatterns) in the query Small list already in memory listAccess + allows(), or batchCheck Buttons for a page of results ("can edit?") batchCheck with that permission Share dialog or access review whoHasAccess with permission and expandGroups One object, one request check

docs.title: TypeScript SDK
docs.text:
permio is the official TypeScript/JavaScript client for the perms.io API. It wraps the API in a few calls for asking "may this principal do X on this resource?". It also gives you typed errors, retries for idempotent reads and async iterators over list endpoints. The full generated API is there too, as an escape hatch.

  • Runs on Node 18+, edge runtimes and browsers. It talks gRPC-web over fetch.
  • Ships ESM and CommonJS builds with bundled type definitions.
  • Has three runtime dependencies: @bufbuild/protobuf, @connectrpc/connect and @connectrpc/connect-web.

Versions

Batch checks, groups and access queries are available from 0.2.0 (npm).

docs.title: Install
docs.text: npm install permio

docs.title: Create a client
docs.text:
import { Permio } from "permio";

const permio = new Permio({
  apiKey: process.env.PERMIO_API_KEY!,
  project: "default", // default project for the helpers below
});

The constructor checks the API key's format and checksum straight away. A mistyped or truncated key throws PermioConfigError before any request is sent. See API keys for the format.

Keep API keys on the server

The SDK works in browsers, but an API key in a browser bundle is visible to anyone who loads the page. Call perms.io from your backend, route handlers or middleware.

docs.title: Options
Checking permissions
docs.text:
All the check helpers take the same parameters (CheckParams):

Parameter Description principal Required. The ID of the user, service or other principal being checked. resource / resources One resource URI, or several. Every resource is checked. permission / permissions One permission name, or several. project Project to check in. Defaults to the client's project. signal An AbortSignal that cancels the call. timeoutMs Overall deadline for this call in ms, across retries. headers Extra request headers.

You can pass both the singular and the plural form; they are merged. Duplicates are removed before sending. A single check accepts up to 100 resources and 100 permissions.

docs.title: check
docs.text:
Resolves to true when the principal holds every permission on every resource:

import { resource } from "permio";

const allowed = await permio.check({
  principal: "alice",
  resource: resource("documents", 42), // "/documents/42"
  permission: "document.read",
});

A principal that lacks the permission is a normal answer: check resolves to false. It only throws when the call itself fails, for example because of a bad key, malformed input or network trouble.

docs.title: checkDetailed
docs.text:
Same question, but it also tells you what is missing, per resource and in request order:

const { allowed, missing } = await permio.checkDetailed({
  principal: "alice",
  resources: ["/documents/1", "/documents/2"],
  permissions: ["document.read", "document.write"],
});
// allowed: false
// missing: [{ resource: "/documents/2", permissions: ["document.write"] }]

missing is an array of { resource: string; permissions: string[] } (MissingPermission), and is empty when allowed is true.

docs.title: assert
docs.text:
Resolves when the principal is allowed and throws PermioDeniedError when it is not. The error carries principal and missing:

await permio.assert({ principal: "alice", resource: "/documents/1", permission: "document.write" });

docs.title: checkAny
docs.text:
Resolves to true when, on every resource, the principal holds at least one of the permissions. It is still a single API call:

await permio.checkAny({
  principal: "alice",
  resource: "/documents/1",
  permissions: ["document.admin", "document.write"],
});

docs.title: checkAll
docs.text: An alias of check: every permission on every resource.

docs.title: Batch checks
docs.text:
Available from 0.2.0

check gives one answer for all its resources together. batchCheck answers each resource separately, which is what you need to filter a list or decide which rows get an "edit" button.

docs.title: batchCheck
docs.text:
Resolves to a Map<string, boolean> from resource URI to allowed, with one entry per distinct resource, in request order:

import { resource } from "permio";

const uris = docs.map((d) => resource("documents", d.id));
const allowed: Map<string, boolean> = await permio.batchCheck({
  principal: "alice",
  resources: uris,
  permission: "document.read",
});
const visible = docs.filter((d) => allowed.get(resource("documents", d.id)));

docs.title: batchCheckDetailed
docs.text:
Same question, but resolves to a BatchCheckEntry[] in request order:

const entries = await permio.batchCheckDetailed({
  principal: "alice",
  resources: ["/documents/1", "/documents/2"],
  permissions: ["document.read", "document.write"],
});
// [
//   { resource: "/documents/1", allowed: true, missing: [] },
//   { resource: "/documents/2", allowed: false, missing: ["document.write"] },
// ]

BatchCheckParams:

Parameter Description principal Required. The principal being checked. resources Required. Resource URIs, each answered separately. Duplicates are sent once. More than 100 are split into several calls, sent in parallel. permission / permissions One or several permission names, up to 100. A resource is allowed only with all of them. project, signal, timeoutMs, headers As for check.

The SDK fails closed: if the API's answer doesn't have exactly one result for each requested resource, it throws a PermioError instead of guessing.

docs.title: Groups
docs.text:
Available from 0.2.0

A group is a named set of principals in a project. Grant to the group's principal ID, group:<slug>, and every member holds the grant. Checks include the principal's groups automatically.

docs.title: group(slug)
docs.text:
Returns the group's principal ID. It throws PermioValidationError unless the slug is 1–64 lower-case letters, digits and hyphens.

import { group } from "permio";

group("editors"); // "group:editors"

await permio.groups.create("editors", { description: "Can edit every document" });
await permio.groups.addMembers("editors", ["alice", "bob"]);

await permio.permissions.grantUserPermissionsAndRolesOnResource({
  projectName: "default",
  userId: group("editors"),
  resourceUri: "/documents",
  permissions: ["document.write"],
});

await permio.check({ principal: "alice", resource: "/documents/42", permission: "document.write" }); // true

docs.title: permio.groups
docs.text:
Every method that takes a group accepts its slug ("editors") or its principal ID ("group:editors").

Method Resolves to create(name, { description? }) Group. Throws a PermioError with code Code.AlreadyExists if the project already has a group with this name. get(name) Group. Throws PermioNotFoundError if it doesn't exist. update(name, { description }) Group. Replaces the description; a group can't be renamed. Throws PermioNotFoundError if it doesn't exist. delete(name) void. Deletes the group, its memberships and every grant made to it. Resolves whether or not it existed. list({ search? }) Async iterator of Group, ordered by name. addMembers(name, principals) AddMembersResult: { added: string[]; existing: string[] }, in request order. removeMembers(name, principals) RemoveMembersResult: { removed: string[]; notMembers: string[] }, in request order. listMembers(name) Async iterator of GroupMember (principalId, createdAt), ordered by principal ID. listForPrincipal(principal) Async iterator of the Groups the principal is a member of, ordered by name.
  • addMembers and removeMembers take 1–100 principals; duplicates are removed. addMembers rejects group: IDs with PermioValidationError, because groups can't contain groups.
  • Every method also takes project, signal, timeoutMs and headers. The list methods take pageSize too, and their timeoutMs and headers apply to each page.
  • Group has id, organisationId, projectName, name, description, principalId ("group:<name>"), createdAt and updatedAt.
const { added, existing } = await permio.groups.addMembers("group:editors", ["alice", "carol"]);

for await (const m of permio.groups.listMembers("editors")) console.log(m.principalId);
for await (const g of permio.groups.listForPrincipal("alice")) console.log(g.name);

Reading groups works with a check-access API key. Creating, updating and deleting groups and changing members needs a key with full access, and changing members also needs the right to grant across the project. See Permissions you need.

docs.title: Access queries
docs.text:
Available from 0.2.0

These answer "where?" and "who?" rather than "may they?". The Filtering lists and building share dialogs guide shows them in context.

docs.title: listAccess
docs.text:
Answers "where may this principal use this permission, at or below under?". It follows every page and resolves to an AccessScopes object:

import { type AccessScopes } from "permio";

const access: AccessScopes = await permio.listAccess({
  principal: "alice",
  permission: "document.read",
  under: "/documents",
});

if (access.coversAll) {
  // alice may read everything under /documents
} else {
  console.log(access.toPrefixes()); // e.g. ["/documents/4", "/documents/7"]
}

ListAccessParams:

Parameter Description principal Required. Access through roles and groups counts. permission Required. One permission name. under Required. Only resources at or below this URI are considered. A _ segment here is literal. project, pageSize, signal, timeoutMs, headers As for the list helpers: timeoutMs and headers apply to each page.

AccessScopes:

Member Type Description under string The URI that was asked about. coversAll boolean The principal holds the permission on under itself, so on everything below it. scopes is then a single subtree scope for under. scopes readonly AccessScopeInfo[] { uri, kind }, ordered by URI. kind is "subtree", "pattern", "exact" (reserved, not returned today) or "unknown" (a kind this SDK version doesn't know; it never matches). isEmpty boolean No access anywhere under under. allows(uri) boolean Whether uri is covered. Matches per segment: /a/b covers /a/b/c but not /a/bc. Malformed URIs are never allowed. toPrefixes() string[] The subtree URIs, for prefix filters. Prefixes covered by a shorter one are dropped. Pattern scopes aren't included. patterns() string[] The pattern URIs, with _ segments. hasPatterns boolean Some scope is a pattern, so toPrefixes() alone doesn't cover everything. exact() string[] The exact URIs. Empty today. toRegExp() RegExp One anchored regular expression matching exactly what allows() accepts. Usable in MongoDB $regex and, via .source, PostgreSQL ~. Matches nothing when there are no scopes.

Warning

A prefix p from toPrefixes() means p and everything below it. Filter with path = p OR path starts with p + "/", never a bare "starts with p", which would let /documents/1 match /documents/12. In SQL, use starts_with(path, p || '/') rather than LIKE, where _ is a wildcard.

For a URI outside under, allows() returning false means "not asked", not "denied". The API key needs permission.check on under and principal.assignment.get on the principal.

docs.title: whoHasAccess
docs.text:
Answers "who has access to this resource?". It follows every page and resolves to an AccessEntry[], ordered by principal ID:

import { type AccessEntry } from "permio";

const entries: AccessEntry[] = await permio.whoHasAccess({
  resource: "/documents/42",
  permission: "document.read",
  expandGroups: true,
});
// [
//   { principal: "alice", isGroup: false, viaGroup: undefined,
//     via: [{ resource: "/documents", inherited: true, match: "ancestor",
//             source: { type: "role", id: "ROLE_ID", name: "viewer" } }] },
//   { principal: "bob", isGroup: false, viaGroup: "editors", via: [...] },
//   { principal: "group:editors", isGroup: true, viaGroup: undefined, via: [...] },
// ]

WhoHasAccessParams:

Parameter Description resource Required. The resource to look at. A _ segment here is literal. permission Optional. Only count grants that confer this permission, so a principal is listed exactly when check() passes for it through its own grants (or, for entries with viaGroup, through that group). Unset, any grant counts. expandGroups Optional. Also list every member of each listed group, once per group, with viaGroup set. project, pageSize, signal, timeoutMs, headers As for the list helpers: timeoutMs and headers apply to each page.

AccessEntry has principal, isGroup, viaGroup (a group slug, or undefined) and via, the grants that give the access, most specific first. Each grant (AccessGrantInfo) has:

  • resource: the URI the grant was made on (the resource, an ancestor, or a _ wildcard URI that matches it);
  • inherited: true unless the grant was made on exactly the resource;
  • match: "exact", "ancestor", "wildcard" or "unknown";
  • source: { type: "role", id, name }, { type: "direct" } for directly granted permissions, or { type: "unknown" }.

The API key needs principal.list and principal.assignment.list on the project.

docs.title: Resource URIs
docs.text: Resource URIs are paths such as /projects/p1/documents/42. A grant on a URI also covers every URI beneath it. See Resources and inheritance for the full rules.

docs.title: resource(...segments)
docs.text:
Builds a URI from raw segments. It adds the leading / and percent-encodes each segment, so an ID that contains /, spaces or other reserved characters stays a single segment:

import { resource } from "permio";

resource("projects", "p1", "documents", 42); // "/projects/p1/documents/42"
resource("files", "reports/2026.pdf");       // "/files/reports%2F2026.pdf"

On top of encodeURIComponent, it also encodes ! ' ( ) *, because the API rejects ( ) * in segments. Empty segments throw PermioValidationError.

Tip

Build URIs the same way when you grant and when you check, or they will not match.

docs.title: Other helpers
docs.text:
Export Description encodeSegment(segment) Encodes one segment the way resource() does. assertResourceUri(uri) Throws PermioValidationError unless uri has the basic shape the API accepts: a leading /, no empty segments, no whitespace or control characters, and at most 2048 bytes. MAX_RESOURCE_URI_LENGTH 2048.

Every check runs assertResourceUri on its URIs before sending. The API enforces the remaining rules, such as no ( ) [ ] { } * + ? | ^ $ \ in segments, and answers with InvalidArgument, which the SDK raises as PermioValidationError.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
Every error the SDK throws extends PermioError. It has these properties:

  • code: the gRPC status Code. Code is re-exported from permio.
  • codeName: the code's name in lower case, for example "permission_denied".
  • metadata: the response headers and trailers.
  • cause: the original error, usually a ConnectError.
Class When PermioConfigError Bad client setup: a malformed API key, no project, an invalid baseUrl or no fetch. PermioAuthError Unauthenticated: the key is missing, unknown or invalidated. PermioPermissionError PermissionDenied: the API key lacks the rights for this call. missing lists what it lacks when the API says. PermioValidationError InvalidArgument, or the SDK's own input checks (for example a URI without a leading /). PermioNotFoundError NotFound, for example getPermission for a name that does not exist. PermioUnavailableError Unavailable, including network failures. PermioTimeoutError DeadlineExceeded, including the SDK's own timeouts. PermioDeniedError Thrown only by assert(), when the principal is not allowed. Has principal and missing.

Any other status is a plain PermioError with the matching code.

Denied is not an error

PermioPermissionError is about the caller. It means your API key is not allowed to make the call: for Check, the key needs permission.check on the checked resources and on the principal. A principal failing a check is a normal result: check() returns false and assert() throws PermioDeniedError.

PermioPermissionError.missing uses the API's fully qualified URIs (/organisation/{org}/project/{project}/...), not the URIs you sent.

import { PermioAuthError, PermioDeniedError, PermioError, PermioPermissionError } from "permio";

try {
  await permio.assert({ principal: "alice", resource: "/documents/1", permission: "document.write" });
} catch (err) {
  if (err instanceof PermioDeniedError) {
    // the principal may not do this: respond with 403
  } else if (err instanceof PermioPermissionError) {
    // the API key may not run this check (it needs permission.check)
    console.error(err.missing);
  } else if (err instanceof PermioAuthError) {
    // the API key is missing, unknown or invalidated
  } else if (err instanceof PermioError) {
    console.error(err.codeName, err.message);
  }
}

toPermioError(error) converts any thrown value into the matching PermioError subclass. parseMissingPermissions(message) extracts the missing list from a PermissionDenied message. You only need these if you build your own transport or client.

docs.title: Retries and timeouts
docs.text:
• Retries: idempotent reads (Check, BatchCheck, and every Get* and List* RPC, including ListAccess, ListPrincipalsWithAccess and the group reads) are retried on Unavailable and DeadlineExceeded. They are retried twice by default, with exponential backoff and jitter. Network failures count as Unavailable.
  • Writes (every Create, Update, Delete, Grant, Revoke, Invite, adding and removing group members, and so on) are never retried.
  • Timeouts:
  • The client's timeoutMs applies to each attempt (default 10 s).
  • A call's timeoutMs is an overall deadline across all attempts.
  • Aborting signal cancels the call and any pending retry.
const permio = new Permio({
  apiKey: process.env.PERMIO_API_KEY!,
  project: "default",
  timeoutMs: 5_000,
  retries: { maxRetries: 3, baseDelayMs: 100, maxDelayMs: 2_000 },
});

await permio.check({ principal: "alice", resource: "/documents/1", permission: "document.read", timeoutMs: 8_000 });

RetryOptions has these fields:

  • maxRetries: retries after the first attempt. Default 2.
  • baseDelayMs: the first delay, which doubles each time. Default 100.
  • maxDelayMs: the cap on a single delay. Default 2000.

isIdempotentMethod("permio.permissions.v1.PermissionsService.Check") tells you whether the SDK retries a given RPC.

docs.title: Listing with iterators
docs.text:
List RPCs are paginated with a cursor (see Pagination). The helpers return async iterators that fetch pages as you go:

for await (const p of permio.listPermissions({ search: "document." })) console.log(p.name);
for await (const role of permio.listRoles()) console.log(role.name, role.permissions.length);
for await (const id of permio.listPrincipals()) console.log(id);
for await (const a of permio.listAssignments({ principal: "alice" })) console.log(a.resourceUri, a.roles);
Method Yields listPermissions(params?) Permission listRoles(params?) Role (with its permissions) listPrincipals(params?) string principal IDs that have grants in the project listAssignments({ principal, ... }) Assignment (resourceUri, permissions, roles) groups.list(params?) Group (from 0.2.0; see Groups) groups.listMembers(name, params?) GroupMember (from 0.2.0) groups.listForPrincipal(principal, params?) Group (from 0.2.0)

Each method takes these parameters:

  • project
  • pageSize: 1–100, default 100
  • signal: stops iteration and any in-flight request
  • timeoutMs: per page
  • headers

listPermissions, listRoles and listPrincipals also take search, which filters by name.

For any other list RPC, use paginate, which follows next_cursor until the API returns an empty one:

import { paginate } from "permio";

for await (const key of paginate(
  (pagination, signal) =>
    permio.organisations.listAPIKeys({ organisationId: "your-org-id", projectName: "default", pagination }, { signal }),
  (res) => res.apiKeys,
)) {
  console.log(key.name);
}

docs.title: Raw clients (full API)
docs.text:
permio.permissions and permio.organisations are the generated Connect clients for permio.permissions.v1.PermissionsService and permio.organisation.v1.OrganisationService. Authentication, timeouts, retries and error mapping are already applied. Every RPC in the API reference is available, with request and response types generated from the protobuf definitions. Method names are the RPC names in lower camel case, and fields are camelCase:

await permio.permissions.createPermission({
  projectName: "default",
  name: "document.read",
  description: "Read documents",
});

const role = await permio.permissions.createRole({
  projectName: "default",
  name: "viewer",
  permissions: ["document.read"], // permission names
});

await permio.permissions.grantUserPermissionsAndRolesOnResource({
  projectName: "default",
  userId: "alice",
  resourceUri: "/documents",
  roles: [role.id], // role IDs
});

const res = await permio.permissions.check({
  projectName: "default",
  principalId: "alice",
  resourceUris: ["/documents/42"],
  permissions: ["document.read"],
});
console.log(res.passed, res.missingPermissions);

What a key can call

By default an API key has check access: it can run checks and access queries, and read permissions, roles, principals, assignments and groups. Creating, updating or deleting permissions, roles and groups, granting or revoking, and changing group members needs a key with full access. See API keys.

The generated messages are exported as the namespaces permissionsv1, organisationv1 and paginationv1. The service descriptors are exported as PermissionsService and OrganisationService:

import { create } from "@bufbuild/protobuf";
import { permissionsv1 } from "permio";

const req = create(permissionsv1.CheckPermissionRequestSchema, { projectName: "default" });

docs.title: API key helpers
docs.text:
Export Description validateApiKey(key) Returns "opaque" for perms_ keys and "jwt" for legacy JWT keys. Throws PermioConfigError if the key is malformed. isValidApiKey(key) true if validateApiKey would pass. API_KEY_LENGTH 44.

These only check the shape and checksum. Only the API can tell you whether a key exists and is still valid.

docs.title: Express
docs.text:
import express, { type RequestHandler } from "express";
import { Permio, PermioDeniedError, resource } from "permio";

const permio = new Permio({ apiKey: process.env.PERMIO_API_KEY!, project: "default" });
const app = express();

const can = (permission: string): RequestHandler => async (req, res, next) => {
  try {
    await permio.assert({
      principal: res.locals.userId, // set by your auth middleware
      resource: resource("documents", req.params.id!),
      permission,
    });
    next();
  } catch (err) {
    if (err instanceof PermioDeniedError) {
      res.status(403).json({ error: "forbidden" });
      return;
    }
    next(err); // any other PermioError: auth, validation, network...
  }
};

app.get("/documents/:id", can("document.read"), (req, res) => {
  res.json({ id: req.params.id });
});

docs.title: Next.js
docs.text:
Create one client and import it on the server only:

// lib/permio.ts
import { Permio } from "permio";

export const permio = new Permio({ apiKey: process.env.PERMIO_API_KEY!, project: "default" });

docs.title: Route handler (App Router)
docs.text:
// app/documents/[id]/route.ts
import { resource } from "permio";
import { permio } from "@/lib/permio";
import { getUserId } from "@/lib/auth"; // your auth

export async function DELETE(_req: Request, { params }: { params: Promise<{ id: string }> }) {
  const { id } = await params;
  const allowed = await permio.check({
    principal: await getUserId(),
    resource: resource("documents", id),
    permission: "document.delete",
  });
  if (!allowed) return new Response("Forbidden", { status: 403 });
  // ...delete the document
  return new Response(null, { status: 204 });
}

docs.title: Middleware
docs.text:
The client only needs fetch, so it also runs in the Edge runtime and in middleware:

// middleware.ts
import { NextResponse, type NextRequest } from "next/server";
import { resource } from "permio";
import { permio } from "@/lib/permio";
import { getUserIdFromRequest } from "@/lib/auth"; // your auth

export async function middleware(req: NextRequest) {
  const userId = await getUserIdFromRequest(req);
  if (!userId) return NextResponse.redirect(new URL("/login", req.url));

  const allowed = await permio.check({
    principal: userId,
    resource: resource("admin"),
    permission: "admin.access",
  });
  return allowed ? NextResponse.next() : new NextResponse("Forbidden", { status: 403 });
}

export const config = { matcher: "/admin/:path*" };

docs.title: How it talks to the API
docs.text: The SDK uses the gRPC-web protocol over fetch (through @connectrpc/connect-web). The perms.io gateway accepts it directly from servers, edge runtimes and browsers. The key is sent as Authorization: Bearer <key>. Timeouts are enforced on the client, so no grpc-timeout header is sent.
